requirements.text: The cloud/ Worker workspace owns all Cloudflare runtime implementation under cloud/src/cloudflare/. Application packages (shared, server, cli, mcp-server, src) reach the cloud service only through pure contracts in @mdt/domain-contracts and JSON/HTTPS. The cloud package imports only @mdt/domain-contracts; it never imports filesystem-aware shared, server, cli, mcp-server, or src. The main application never imports @mdt/cloud.
Concurrent requests sharing one idempotency key return one stable reservation and advance the counter once
Different cloud projects allocate ticket numbers independently
Existing Markdown tickets remain readable and editable during a cloud outage while new cloud-bound creation stays blocked
A real Access-protected environment validates browser and interactive CLI human attribution from a verified email claim
A real Access-protected environment validates service-token machine attribution from a verified common_name claim
Viewer, contributor, and owner permissions are enforced per cloud project for read, reserve, publish, list-members, and manage-members operations
Unauthorized or unknown project references do not disclose project existence; they return the same response as a hidden project
Revoked membership blocks the next protected project operation; there is no authorization cache in the first slice
Acknowledged tickets expose only the approved header projection, never a ticket body
Stale projection writes are rejected through expected-version precondition semantics
The board distinguishes cloud-projected state from canonical local ticket state without implying teammate ownership, presence, or canonical local content
Allocation, projection, membership, denial, and recovery actions produce structured redacted audit records
Disabling cloud binding leaves all durable ticket content usable from Markdown/Git
Reusing one idempotency key with a different canonical request hash returns 409 idempotency_key_reused and does not allocate a new number
Acknowledgement lost after allocation leaves a recoverable reservation that replays with the same reservation id; if abandoned it is marked orphaned and the number is never reused
A scheduled handler marks reserved rows older than 24 hours as abandoned in bounded batches without decrementing the counter or deleting the reservation
The final owner cannot be removed or demoted; a principal cannot grant a role higher than its own
On an unknown kid the Access verifier refreshes JWKS once and retries so key rotation does not require a deployment
Headless adapters refuse to attach service-token headers to any origin not on the operator-controlled allowlist and reject redirects

The coordination database is authoritative for project UUID, membership, ticket-number counter, reservations, idempotency outcomes, projection versions, and audit. Markdown/Git is authoritative for ticket body and projected headers. D1 never writes a projected value back into Markdown.
Ticket numbers are never reused. Abandoned, orphaned, and acknowledged reservations all retain their numbers. The counter is monotonic.
Cloud binding is opt-in per project, enabled only after project provisioning and a successful identity/membership probe.

No Access token, service-token ID/secret, JWT, team domain, or audience tag is permitted in .mdt-config.toml or the global project registry; credentials live only in interactive or backend secret providers.
Rate limiting is only an abuse guard; it must not be used to issue numbers, enforce quotas, or replace D1 unique constraints.
The first slice excludes presence, activity indicators, offline allocation, body sync, WebSockets, and Durable Objects.

The effective trusted-origin set combines distribution-provided HTTPS origins with global fileOnly cloudSync.allowedOrigins extensions; an empty extension list denies custom origins, project files cannot expand trust, and a shipped service does not require per-device project activation.

A cloud-bound create fails recoverably when coordination is unavailable; it never allocates a local fallback number, temporary key, offline range, or lease. This MUST hold through the real TicketService.createCR path (strategy selection), not only the isolated allocator unit test.

Another authorized client sees projected create and status changes within the configured polling interval, proven end-to-end (a local projection poller observing the cloud feed), not only the cloud polling endpoint in isolation.

Concurrent creates through CLI, MCP, and HTTP for one cloud project return unique numbers; a cloud-bound create never writes or acknowledges a second local ticket with an occupied key, including a different slug. Raw filesystem writes are detected as conflicts when observed, not claimed to be impossible.

A failed local Markdown write retries its original reservation and immutable creation identity without number reuse; only a verified replay of the same creation may reuse an existing file. A conflicting held reservation remains explicit recoverable work, never a silent replacement allocation.

Local-only projects with no CONFIG_DIR cloud connection preserve existing allocation, creation, and board behavior and make no cloud call. Enabled connections coordinate; disabled, malformed, or untrusted connections never resume local numbering (MDT-201 cutover).

A fresh cloud-bound create scans canonical ticket identities across the physical repository and known worktrees, fails closed on scan errors or ambiguity, journals its observed minimum number and creation identity, and obtains a coordinator-assigned number at or above that minimum and the authoritative counter. Replay preserves the original allocation inputs and result.

A watched or startup-discovered file in a cloud-bound project is classified as verified same creation, conflict, unmanaged, or verification pending. A key already reserved for another creation is a conflict; missing identity or inaccessible evidence is unverified. Detection preserves the file and emits a bounded actionable diagnostic without automatically reserving, acknowledging, publishing, renumbering, or deleting it.

When multiple local files claim one ticket key, key-based CLI, MCP, and HTTP reads and mutations report ambiguity with authorized relative file paths instead of selecting the first match or changing an unrelated ticket. Files remain available for explicit path-based inspection and operator resolution.

An authorized operator can dry-run and explicitly reconcile an existing cloud project after a collision: preserve allocation history, audit corrections, raise the counter to at least the maximum of its current value, highest retained reservation plus one, and reviewed canonical high-water plus one, and resolve incorrect creation/projection associations before resuming coordination. Repeating a repair is idempotent and never reuses a number.

Ticket number, filename, mutable header equality, event origin, or membership alone does not establish creation identity. New cloud creates persist a non-secret immutable creationId in canonical frontmatter, journal, and the coordinator reservation; its scoped association is verified before cloud publication. Legacy files or journals without evidence remain unverified until explicit audited reconciliation. No secret or active cloud binding is added to repository configuration.

Allocation floor and creationId are immutable idempotency inputs verified by the coordinator, not trusted solely through an opaque client requestHash. Reservation insert, counter advance, idempotency result, and allocation audit stay atomic under differing-floor and operator-repair races. A protocol/capability mismatch fails closed; it never silently ignores the floor or creation identity.

File watchers are observation adapters, not allocation or import authorities. Shared services own classification and identity policy; server adapters preserve physical file identity internally and expose only authorized relative diagnostic paths. Duplicate events are coalesced; failures do not start unbounded cloud probes or interactive authentication.

A manual file uses an already reserved or acknowledged key, copies another creationId, or duplicates a slugged key: reject a proven mismatched association as conflict, retain unknown associations as verification pending, and never infer ownership from the number or overwrite either creation.

Watcher verification encounters unavailable coordination, missing credentials, partial files, permission errors, or repeated events: preserve bytes, retain a deduplicated actionable pending diagnostic, and retry only through a bounded or explicit recovery path without cloud writes.

Git, another process, or a known worktree changes occupied keys during creation or an operator raises the counter after allocation pre-read: recheck identity at write and acknowledgement boundaries, suppress stale reservation inserts transactionally, and surface detected conflicts without silently renumbering. Unseen writes in disconnected clones cannot be guaranteed absent.

scenarios.title: Concurrent creates return unique numbers
scenarios.given: Two contributors each send a create request to one cloud-bound project at the same time
scenarios.when: When the Worker executes both reservation transactions
scenarios.then: Then each receives a distinct ticket number and no duplicate reservation row exists

scenarios.title: Idempotent key replay returns one reservation
scenarios.given: A client sends a reservation request that fails after the Worker allocated, and retries with the same Idempotency-Key and request hash
scenarios.when: When the retry reaches the Worker
scenarios.then: Then the original reservation is returned and the project counter has advanced only once

scenarios.title: Cross-project allocation is independent
scenarios.given: Two cloud projects exist with counters at different values
scenarios.when: When each project processes a create concurrently
scenarios.then: Then each allocates from its own counter and the numbers do not collide

scenarios.title: Failed local write retries the same reservation
scenarios.given: Allocation succeeds but the local Markdown write fails and the operation journal holds the reservation
scenarios.when: When the client retries create
scenarios.then: Then it reuses the same reservation id and acknowledges it without allocating a new number

scenarios.title: Coordination down blocks cloud create
scenarios.given: A cloud-bound project cannot reach the coordination service
scenarios.when: When a create is attempted
scenarios.then: Then it fails recoverably and never assigns a local fallback number, temporary key, range, or lease

scenarios.title: Outage keeps existing tickets usable
scenarios.given: The coordination service is unavailable for a cloud-bound project
scenarios.when: When a client reads or edits an existing Markdown ticket
scenarios.then: Then the operation succeeds while new cloud-bound creation stays blocked

scenarios.title: Local-only projects are unchanged
scenarios.given: A project has no cloud binding
scenarios.when: When a client creates a ticket
scenarios.then: Then allocation uses the existing local highest-plus-one scan and no cloud call is made

scenarios.title: Human email attribution on live Worker
scenarios.given: A human authenticates through Cloudflare Access and calls the coordination API
scenarios.when: When the Worker validates the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion
scenarios.then: Then it maps the verified email as a human principal and the audit records kind=human

scenarios.title: Service-token machine attribution on live Worker
scenarios.given: A headless client presents Access service-token headers
scenarios.when: When Access forwards the assertion to the Worker
scenarios.then: Then it maps the verified common_name as a machine principal and the audit records kind=machine

scenarios.title: Role permissions per project
scenarios.given: A viewer, contributor, and owner each attempt reserve, publish, list-members, and manage-members
scenarios.when: When each operation is authorized
scenarios.then: Then viewer is denied writes, contributor can reserve and publish but not manage members, and owner can do all

scenarios.title: Unknown project is non-disclosing
scenarios.given: A principal requests a project it has no membership in, and a truly nonexistent project
scenarios.when: When the Worker responds
scenarios.then: Then both return the identical 404 project_not_found with no distinguishing detail

scenarios.title: Revoked membership blocks next operation
scenarios.given: An owner revokes a member's role
scenarios.when: When that member's next request reaches the Worker
scenarios.then: Then it is denied with no authorization cache having served a stale grant

scenarios.title: Projection exposes only approved headers
scenarios.given: A ticket is acknowledged and its projection published
scenarios.when: When another client polls projections
scenarios.then: Then it receives only code, title, status, type, priority, assignee, and dates, never the body

scenarios.title: Stale projection write rejected
scenarios.given: A client publishes a projection whose expected version is older than the current version
scenarios.when: When the Worker checks the precondition
scenarios.then: Then it rejects the write and does not overwrite the newer projection

scenarios.title: Another client sees changes via polling
scenarios.given: One client publishes a status change to a projection
scenarios.when: When a second authorized client polls at the configured interval
scenarios.then: Then it observes the change within pollIntervalSeconds

scenarios.title: Board labels projected stubs
scenarios.given: A cloud-projected header exists for a ticket with no canonical local file
scenarios.when: When the board renders
scenarios.then: Then it shows a clearly labeled read-only stub that implies no teammate ownership or presence

scenarios.title: Actions produce structured redacted audit
scenarios.given: An allocation, projection update, membership change, denial, and recovery each occur
scenarios.when: When each completes
scenarios.then: Then a structured audit record is written to D1 with principal kind and id but no raw token, cookie, or assertion

scenarios.title: Disabling cloud keeps content usable
scenarios.given: A cloud-bound project is suspended and detached per the documented sequence
scenarios.when: When cloud binding is removed
scenarios.then: Then all ticket files remain readable and editable from Markdown/Git

scenarios.title: Idempotency key reused with a different request
scenarios.given: A client reuses an Idempotency-Key with a different canonical request hash
scenarios.when: When the request reaches the Worker
scenarios.then: Then it returns 409 idempotency_key_reused and allocates no new number

scenarios.title: Failed local write retries the same reservation
scenarios.given: Allocation succeeded but neither acknowledgement nor a canonical file ever appears and the reservation ages
scenarios.when: When the client retries create or the scheduled handler runs
scenarios.then: Then it reuses the same reservation id and if retired the number is never reused

scenarios.title: Human email attribution with JWKS refresh
scenarios.given: An assertion arrives with a kid absent from the cached JWKS
scenarios.when: When the verifier refreshes and the human authenticates through Access
scenarios.then: Then it maps the verified email as a human principal and refreshes JWKS once on unknown kid

scenarios.title: Service-token attribution respects origin allowlist
scenarios.given: A headless adapter is asked to send service-token headers to an origin not in cloudSync.allowedOrigins
scenarios.when: When it builds the request to obtain machine attribution
scenarios.then: Then it refuses to attach the headers and rejects any redirect

scenarios.title: Role permissions protect the final owner
scenarios.given: An attempt is made to remove or demote the last owner of a project
scenarios.when: When the Worker authorizes the membership change
scenarios.then: Then it is denied

scenarios.title: Scheduled expiry produces structured audit
scenarios.given: Reserved rows older than 24 hours exist
scenarios.when: When the 15-minute scheduled handler runs
scenarios.then: Then a bounded batch is marked abandoned and an audit record is written without decrementing the counter

scenarios.title: Stale coordinator skips local occupied numbers
scenarios.given: Counter is 258 and canonical local keys extend through 262
scenarios.when: a fresh cloud-bound CLI, MCP, or HTTP create requests allocation
scenarios.then: the coordinator reserves at least 263 and exactly one canonical key is written and acknowledged

scenarios.title: Different slug cannot bypass key uniqueness
scenarios.given: a reservation or recovery intent targets a key occupied by another creation under another slug
scenarios.when: the shared writer attempts creation or acknowledgement
scenarios.then: it reports a recoverable conflict, preserves both existing bytes and the held reservation, and never reports creation success

scenarios.title: Allocation identity and floor remain stable on retry
scenarios.given: a journaled create already has immutable allocation inputs and the counter has subsequently advanced
scenarios.when: the intent is retried or its floor or creation identity is changed under the same idempotency key
scenarios.then: an unchanged retry returns the original reservation without advancing; changed immutable inputs are rejected

scenarios.title: Manual file cannot adopt another creation reservation
scenarios.given: a manually added file uses a key already reserved or acknowledged for a different proven creation
scenarios.when: the watcher or startup inventory classifies the file
scenarios.then: it retains the file, reports conflict, and makes no reservation, acknowledgement, projection, rename, or delete mutation

scenarios.title: Missing evidence does not imply ownership
scenarios.given: a local file has no verifiable creation provenance or coordination evidence cannot be read
scenarios.when: the file is observed
scenarios.then: the file remains inspectable with an unmanaged or verification-pending diagnostic and no automatic cloud mutation

scenarios.title: Git delivery of a verified ticket is not a new create
scenarios.given: a ticket arrives through Git with creationId matching its acknowledged coordinator claim
scenarios.when: the watcher or startup inventory observes the file
scenarios.then: it identifies the same existing creation without reserving or acknowledging again

scenarios.title: Key-based adapters refuse ambiguous local tickets
scenarios.given: two local files claim MDT-258
scenarios.when: CLI, MCP, or HTTP resolves MDT-258 for reading or mutation
scenarios.then: it reports ambiguity and authorized relative paths rather than selecting or mutating either file

scenarios.title: Reviewed operator repair advances without number reuse
scenarios.given: coordination is suspended and reviewed files, reservations, projections, and pending intents are inventoried
scenarios.when: an authorized operator previews and applies the explicit repair twice
scenarios.then: the counter never decreases, prior allocation history remains, the second apply is idempotent, and unresolved identity conflicts keep resumption blocked

scenarios.title: An explicit owner action inspects and resumes the original pending creation
scenarios.given: A valid v2 creation journal survives a process exit with its original draft, identity, floor and reservation
scenarios.when: The owner inspects it and explicitly resumes it through a shipped adapter without reconstructing create arguments
scenarios.then: The shared recovery service verifies the current file and held reservation, reuses the original intent, acknowledges at most once and retains evidence on failure

scenarios.title: Legacy or corrupt journals remain inspectable and require reviewed resolution
scenarios.given: An active or legacy routing location contains a legacy, corrupt or schema-invalid creation journal
scenarios.when: The owner requests inspection or a new create is attempted
scenarios.then: Inspection reports bounded redacted state, original routing and remediation; no automatic deletion, identity invention, replacement reservation or startup write occurs; reconciliation requires explicit reviewed proof and expected journal state

scenarios.title: Uncertain lock ownership is inspectable without stealing a live lock
scenarios.given: A retained creation lock has an ambiguous owner or a PID now belonging to another process
scenarios.when: The owner inspects recovery state or attempts explicit resume
scenarios.then: The outcome reports available PID and creation time and a safe verification path; age alone never authorizes lock theft and no overlapping create runs

scenarios.title: Lowercase local project codes use the canonical cloud key consistently
scenarios.given: A supported local project config spells its code mdt and is connected to cloud project code MDT
scenarios.when: A supported create and its same-intent recovery run
scenarios.then: The canonical project/key identity is consistent before reservation, writing and verification; creation succeeds with strict Worker identity checks and no automatic renaming of existing files

scenarios.title: Incomplete inventory preserves fail-closed safety and actionable diagnostics
scenarios.given: A known worktree is unavailable, a canonical root is unreadable or a filename contains an unsupported number
scenarios.when: Inventory is used by create or explicit observation
scenarios.then: Creation stays blocked and available inventory evidence is retained; diagnostics name authorized relative paths, typed causes and safe operator steps without silently skipping roots or mutating files

scenarios.title: Bounded rotation preserves last verified evidence for unchanged files
scenarios.given: More than64 eligible canonical creations have matching acknowledged cloud claims
scenarios.when: Repeated event-triggered observations rotate a maximum64 claim probes per pass
scenarios.then: An unchanged file is not demoted solely because it is outside this pass; last verification and freshness remain explicit, duplicate notifications are coalesced and no timer or cloud mutation is added

scenarios.title: Cached claim evidence cannot outlive a meaningful identity or connection change
scenarios.given: Last verified claim evidence exists for a file in a particular local project, binding and principal context
scenarios.when: The file identity changes, a duplicate appears, the binding or principal changes, or a probe returns an authorization failure
scenarios.then: Affected cached evidence is invalidated or explicitly stale; a previous verified outcome cannot authorize adoption or publication, and current membership remains enforced on mutations

obligations.title: Cloud package boundary: cloud/ owns Worker runtime; app packages reach it only via JSON/HTTPS over @mdt/domain-contracts
Access JWT validation and principal mapping: RS256 JWKS verify, human/machine principal, no secrets in config
Membership authorization: per-project roles, non-disclosure, revocation, no authz cache
Local orchestration: project binding selects local or durable cloud create; journal recovery; origin allowlist; local-only preserved
Versioned header projection: one-way publish, precondition conflicts, polling cursor, board distinction
Operations: migrations, scheduled maintenance, redacted audit, rate-limit abuse guard, disable/vendor-exit
Static allocation batch uses immutable floor and creation identity, suppresses stale inserts before mutation, and atomically preserves uniqueness, replay, monotonic counter, and non-reuse
Shared identity scan, journal, writer, and recovery verify immutable creation provenance, reject key ambiguity, and preserve transport-independent behavior

Shared classification receives path-preserving watcher and startup observations, distinguishes verified, conflict, unmanaged, and pending states, and produces bounded diagnostics without automatic adoption
Explicit authorized operator repair previews changes, retains allocation history, audits monotonic idempotent correction, and resolves creation/projection associations before resumption
Explicit owner-invoked creation inspection/resume and reviewed legacy resolution preserve identity, original receipts and exclusive safe lock ownership
Canonical project/key identity is consistent across supported config spelling, shared create, immutable recovery and strict Worker checks
Incomplete inventory remains fail-closed with actionable per-path evidence and bounded claim rotation preserves last verified evidence with freshness and safe invalidation
Route initial acknowledgement through the existing serialized hub with prearmed recovery and committed-row delivery
